subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core logical-action idempotency contract for sub-agent side effects, and if so where should the claim/replay state live?
rationale: Current code already fixes narrower message-tool retries, but the requested behavior crosses core subagent lifecycle, gateway/API idempotency, tool/plugin boundaries, persisted state, and third-party side effects, so automation cannot choose the permanent contract safely.

options.title: Design core logical-action idempotency
options.body: Keep this issue open as the planning thread for a server-side claim/commit/replay model keyed by session, sub-agent, action type, target, payload digest, and expiry.

options.title: Limit core to built-in delivery paths
options.body: Declare that OpenClaw only guarantees idempotency for gateway/message-tool/known delivery surfaces and document external POST idempotency as tool or skill responsibility.

options.title: Move this to plugin or skill guidance
options.body: Treat generalized third-party side-effect dedupe as a ClawHub skill/plugin pattern unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design core logical-action idempotency
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the planning thread for a server-side claim/commit/replay model keyed by session, sub-agent, action type, target, payload digest, and expiry.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the product boundary for core sub-agent side-effect semantics, and steipete is the strongest available current-main routing signal from the inspected history.
